note: Owns his own marketing agency, formerly at Nike — squarely the 'already successful' profile — and he is the purest good-to-great case in the batch, self-rating 'a very solid eight' and buying the last two points. He is the opposite of deconditioned: an ultra-distance runner mid-build for a 230 km race. The two misses are instructive. Health is not his neglected area, it is his most heavily invested one — he already funds a nutritionist, an exercise physiologist, a running coach and a therapist, so the offer arrives as a fifth specialist competing with four incumbents rather than as the fix for a neglected domain. And on income the stated criterion did not hold: he said 'this represents way more than I wanted to do', proposed revisiting in four or five months, and ultimately bought a $1,200 trial rather than a $6,000 programme. This is the mirror image of the Robyn Stillwater case in the reference set — there, someone outside the ICP closed at full price; here, someone who reads as ICP on profile closed at a fifth of it. The pattern in both is that the stated income criterion is not predicting what people actually pay.
